memory_candidates.content: When a fixture-based suite proves a lint's own output round-trips through a downstream extraction helper (verify_deploy_extract_verdict_lines or similar anchored line-selector), compare the selected count against the PRODUCER's own authoritative summary count (e.g. a 'Total violations: N' line), never a raw substring grep -c over the full captured output. A fixture deliberately constructed to trigger the lint can legitimately re-quote the detection token inside its own source text, which a raw substring count over-counts (the re-quoted text appears on a second physical line after an embedded literal \n in the fixture is rendered as an actual newline by the lint's own echo -e). The summary-line count is immune to this and is the correct ground truth for a self-referential round-trip assertion.

git-commit-scoped.sh (and wrappers over it) stage per-file, not per-hunk. When two concurrently-dispatched tasks both declare the same file in file_scope, whichever commits first captures the WHOLE current diff of that file, silently absorbing the other task's still-uncommitted edits under its own unrelated commit message (observed live: a sibling's gate16 WARN-FINDING commit absorbed this task's gate25_run()/--only-gate bound fix with zero mention in its message). Per git-workflow.md, do not amend or rewrite the foreign commit to fix attribution. Instead: re-check git status --short on every shared file immediately before your own phase commit (this already catches the case where the file is clean because a sibling committed it first), commit only the files that remain dirty for your own task, and cite the foreign commit's SHA in your own commit message or handoff for provenance.
